standard_prerequisites.name: Pointwise one step devissage, its finite-presentation and flatness behaviour, and the affine base change of complete devissages
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemma lemma-elementary-devissage-variant (05H6, line 855), Lemma lemma-existence-alpha (05HF, line 1138), Lemma lemma-elementary-etale-neighbourhood (05HE, line 1027) and Lemma lemma-base-change-complete-at-x (05HK, line 1313)
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the four inputs of the induction step: the one step devissage after elementary etale localisation, the free cover alpha_1 with a strictly smaller cokernel on the fibre, the diagram that transports a one step devissage up to a complete one, and the affine base change of the existing complete devissage.

core_obligations: Run the induction on d = dim_x Supp(F_s): apply the elementary-devissage variant to reduce to the case where F/X/S carries a one step devissage (Z_1, Y_1, i_1, pi_1, G_1) at x, then apply the alpha lemma to get alpha_1 : O_{Y_1}^{\oplus r_1} -> pi_{1,*}G_1 whose fibre at the generic point xi_1 of Y_1 over s is an isomorphism and with dim_{y_1} Supp(Coker(alpha_1)_s) < d; if the stalk of Coker(alpha_1)_s at y_1 vanishes, shrink Y_1 by the shrinking lemma so that Coker(alpha_1) = 0 and obtain a complete devissage of length zero (proof lines 1447-1484).

Induction step in the non-vanishing case: apply the induction hypothesis to Coker(alpha_1) on Y_1 to obtain a pointed elementary etale neighbourhood (Y'_1, y'_1) -> (Y_1, y_1) over (S', s') and a complete devissage (Z_k, Y_k, i_k, pi_k, G_k, alpha_k, z_k, y_k)_{k=2..n} of h^*Coker(alpha_1)/Y'_1/S' at y'_1, then apply the elementary etale neighbourhood lemma to the system (Z_1, Y_1, i_1, pi_1, G_1) and to the displayed diagram, and base change the complete devissage of part two to S'' so that the two devissages now live over the same data, recording the four resulting assumptions (a)-(d) (proof lines 1487-1547).

Glue the two devissages by a two-stage shrinking: use the complete shrinking lemma's item on X to find a standard shrinking S', X'_1, Z'_2, Y'_2, ..., Y'_n of the devissage (d) with X'_1 contained in Y_1, note X'_1 is then a standard open of the affine Y_1, shrink the base of the one step devissage (a) to S' and then shrink again using the item on Y so that eventually Y''_1 = X'_1 x_S S'' with S'' contained in S', and conclude that Z''_1, Y''_1, Z'_2 x_{S'} S'', Y'_2 x_{S'} S'', ..., Y'_n x_{S'} S'' is the required complete devissage (proof lines 1548-1569).
proof_roadmap: Induction setup: induct on d = dim_x Supp(F_s), first replacing the pair by an elementary etale neighbourhood on which F has a one step devissage at x (proof lines 1447-1464).

Dimension-reducing step: the alpha lemma produces alpha_1 : O_{Y_1}^{\oplus r_1} -> pi_{1,*}G_1 with dim_{y_1} Supp(Coker(alpha_1)_s) < d; if the stalk at y_1 vanishes, shrink Y_1 to get Coker(alpha_1) = 0 and a length-zero complete devissage, and otherwise the induction hypothesis applies to the cokernel on Y_1 (proof lines 1466-1485).

Fitting the pieces over one base: the resulting complete devissage of h^*Coker(alpha_1)/Y'_1/S' is base changed to S'' and the elementary etale neighbourhood lemma is applied to the one step devissage, producing the situation (a)-(d) in which the two devissages are separated (proof lines 1487-1547).

Final shrinking: shrink the complete devissage so that X'_1 lies inside Y_1, then shrink the one step devissage so that Y''_1 = X'_1 x_S S'' with S'' inside S', and read off the complete devissage of F/X/S at x (proof lines 1548-1569).
difficulty_reason: The proposition produces, for X locally of finite type over S and a point x over s, a pointed elementary etale neighbourhood diagram such that the pullback of F over X'/S' has a complete devissage at x, and the proof is an induction on d = dim_x Supp(F_s) whose step is a genuine construction rather than a citation (statement lines 1433-1443; proof lines 1447-1464). The dimension descent is driven by the free cover alpha_1 : O_{Y_1}^{\oplus r_1} -> pi_{1,*}G_1, whose cokernel on the fibre has support of strictly smaller dimension at y_1, so the induction hypothesis can be invoked either on Y_1 (non-vanishing stalk) or, after a shrinking that kills the cokernel, to give the length-zero case (proof lines 1466-1485). The part that cannot be done routinely is the final gluing: the one step devissage of F and the complete devissage of the cokernel produced over different elementary etale neighbourhoods S' and S'' have to be made to live over a single base, which is done by a two-stage shrinking in which X'_1 is first pushed inside Y_1 and then the one step devissage is shrunk so that Y''_1 = X'_1 x_S S'' with S'' contained in S' (proof lines 1548-1569); the author explicitly invites the reader to carry out this step independently rather than read it. This combination of a dimension-descending induction with a nested shrinking of two devissages is the independent technical content of the chapter's existence theorem.
